title: Does Verifier Feedback Reduce Residual Unsafe Vendor-CLI Configurations? A Preregistered Paired Fault-Injection Study
abstract: We report a preregistered, controlled-challenge paired evaluation of verifier-guided repair for LLM-generated vendor CLI templates. Under the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing semantics (preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1), we executed 40 planned paired tasks and analyzed 39 complete pairs (one pair excluded per the preregistered complete-pair rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier + simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired contingency: n11=29, n10=9 (guarded-only), n01=1 (baseline-only), n00=0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (<= planned maximum 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute it were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, clarify execution semantics and mechanisms suggested by per-episode validator traces, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are being evaluated as aides for network operations tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a generated candidate is checked by a deterministic verifier and, if violations appear, verifier diagnostics are fed back to produce a repair. Prior controlled evaluations in code and IaC domains indicate that inserting deterministic verifiers raises verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes and interaction costs [1]–[4]. Field studies caution that read-oriented assistance does not automatically yield safe closed-loop changes in NetOps [5].

This paper asks a narrowly scoped, preregistered question under a controlled-challenge design: when the same deterministically injected actionable fault is presented to two matched repair episodes (shared controlled-fault candidate), does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the repair model reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair? The shared-candidate paired design isolates the effect of diagnostics exposure while ensuring the intervention is activated for every task.
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair architectures have empirical support for improving verifier-detected pass rates in code, IaC, and DSL benchmarks: deterministic verifiers interposed between stochastic generation and acceptance often raise pass@1/validator-pass metrics and supplying verifier diagnostics to repair models typically increases the chance a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck [1], [2]. Complementary controlled analyses document important caveats: single-proxy verifier loops can be exploited (optimization toward the proxy degrades the true target property), and verifier mediation imposes measurable interaction and compute overheads (the "verifier tax") that depend on design choices [3], [4]. Surveys and field case studies specific to NetOps/AIOps indicate LLMs deliver useful read-oriented assistance, but evidence for safe autonomous remediation at production scale is currently limited [5].

These prior results motivate our controlled fault-injection paired experiment: (a) use deterministic faults that guarantee verifier activation (so the treatment—exposing diagnostics—can act), (b) adopt shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing to match source generation across arms, and (c) require agreement between a deterministic validator and a simulator for the primary success predicate to limit verifier/simulator mismatch risks.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a binary success indicator requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance check to accept the post-repair configuration.

Adapter, pairing, and sampling semantics. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under that contract exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate was produced per task index and that same candidate was reused unchanged by both arms; exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both conditions. Baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed); guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Controlled-challenge bank and scoring. We used a deterministic controlled-fault generator to produce 40 preregistered task indices with realistic actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change, unintended_state_change). The primary success predicate required agreement between the deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-backed compliance check. The preregistration froze a harmful-change labeling mapping that marks episodes harmful if post-repair validator traces include PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; that mapping and all per-episode validation traces were recorded during execution to permit deterministic reaggregation of the preregistered safety statistic.

Execution and analysis plan. The confirmatory model was declared as gpt-5-mini, with a total model-call budget of 120 for the run. The predefined primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent). We reported discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable). All per-episode traces and scored artifacts required for recomputation were archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; complete_pair_count = 39 (one pair excluded because its source generation was unscorable under the preregistered rule). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source_generation_attempt_count = 40 with source_valid_count = 39 and source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (n = 39 complete pairs). Baseline success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Missingness and preregistered safety aggregation. One pair was excluded per the preregistered complete-pair rule; terminal error reasons were recorded. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation is not present in the archived confirmatory summary produced during the execution; therefore a confirmatory safety verdict is unresolved here. The frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validator traces required to compute that aggregation were recorded in the archive and permit deterministic independent recomputation; any harmful-overrepair numbers computed outside the archived confirmatory summary are treated as exploratory.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation and precision. The paired design isolates diagnostics exposure because both arms received the same initial controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets under the adapter contract. The observed paired absolute increase of ~20.5 percentage points (95% CI ≈ [7.7, 35.9] percentage points) shows a substantial and statistically detectable effect at two-sided alpha = 0.05 despite the preregistered planning target being larger (~30 percentage points). The preregistered planning model anticipated larger detectable effects given n=40; observing a significant ~20.5pp effect reflects the realized discordant-pair structure (n10=9, n01=1) and the study's exact-paired test sensitivity.

Mechanisms suggested by per-episode traces. Per-episode validator traces indicate diagnostics often provided explicit violation codes (e.g., FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE) and contextual metadata (affected_interface, required_command_count). These diagnostics appear to guide targeted edits: guarded repairs frequently show validator_feedback_exposed_to_model = true and, in many discordant episodes where baseline failed and guarded passed (example: task-000003), the guarded repair removed or avoided protected-interface edits and restored required sequences to meet the required final state. Representative artifact examples: task-000003 baseline validation_after contained PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and related violations and scored INVALID, while the guarded repair (validator feedback exposed) corrected the sequence and scored VALID. This pattern—diagnostics translating into focused corrective edits—plausibly explains the predominance of n10 (guarded-only) discordant pairs.

Failure-mode diagnostics and safety boundary. The archived validator traces catalog the principal violation codes observed during confirmatory execution (FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE). These served both as the unit of feedback to the guarded repair model and as the basis for the frozen harmful-change mapping used in the preregistration. Because the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation was not computed in the archived confirmatory summary, we make no confirmatory safety claim here; instead we document that the necessary inputs for that preregistered safety tally (the frozen mapping and per-episode traces) exist in the archive and can deterministically reproduce the planned safety statistic.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Exposing diagnostics materially improved the verifier+simulator-validated success rate on this controlled fault bank, but verifier-guided workflows incur extra model–verifier interactions: confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls. Whether this verifier tax is operationally acceptable depends on deployment-scale cost/latency constraints and remains to be evaluated in larger-scale, multi-model replications.

Threats to validity and generality. Internal validity: because the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset), null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was reused by both arms, so differences isolate diagnostics exposure rather than first-pass generation variation. Construct validity: the primary success predicate required agreement of a deterministic validator and a simulator; both components limit the operational meaning of “valid.” External validity: confirmatory execution used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), one adapter family, and a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank limited to the preregistered 40 indices; results do not by themselves establish generalization across vendors, models, or naturalistic operator streams. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 yields reasonable precision for the observed contrast but limits power for subgroup or per-fault-class inference.

Recommended next steps. Deterministic reaggregation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic from the archived traces is a priority before any operational recommendation. Follow-up replications should run multi-model and multi-verifier ensembles, report model-call cost/latency tradeoffs at scale, and evaluate whether explicit harmful-change constraints and multi-verifier designs reduce residual safety risk and verifier-exploitation in longer-horizon agentic workflows.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow increased verifier+simulator-validated configuration success by an absolute ~20.51 percentage points (p = 0.021484375; 95% CI ≈ [0.0769, 0.3590]) on the preregistered synthetic task bank using the declared model gpt-5-mini. The result is bounded by the controlled fault bank, single-model adapter, deterministic validator/simulator scoring, and the pairing semantics that reuse the same initial candidate across arms. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation was not computed in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validation traces recorded during execution permit deterministic independent recomputation. We recommend deterministic safety reaggregation, multi-model and multi-verifier replications, and deployment-scale cost/latency evaluations before operational adoption of verifier-guided closed-loop repairs in NetOps settings.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
